name: JaredFromSubway MEV Bot

descriptions.text: JaredFromSubway MEV bot was exploited, resulting in a loss of 4,424 ETH (~$7.5M). Analysis: https://www.certik.com/blog/jaredfromsubway-mev-bot-incident-analysis Source: https://twitter.com/CertiKAlert/status/2070478621139935316

The MEV bot operated by JaredFromSubway.eth was drained of approximately $7.5 million. Attackers deployed fake token wrappers and liquidity pools to trick the bot’s automated MEV execution system into granting token approvals to attacker-controlled contracts. They then exploited the unrevoked approvals to transfer out WETH, USDC, and USDT via transferFrom. It was not a traditional phishing attack or a vulnerability in the victim contracts themselves, but a flaw in the bot’s automated approval-generation mechanism. Jared publicly offered a $1 million bounty for full recovery with full confidentiality.

On June 20, 2026, the JaredFromSubway MEV bot on Ethereum was drained of about $7.5 million in WETH, USDC, and USDT. The attacker constructed a honeypot of fake token contracts and pools, tricking the bot into approving tokens without consuming allowances. These unspent approvals were drained in a single sweep. The bot's automated trading logic granted token approvals to untrusted, attacker-controlled wrapper contracts and pools without verifying that allowances were actually consumed after trades. These standing permissions persisted, accumulating open exposures that the attacker harvested in a single batch transaction.
